conclusion: The quantum ADMM algorithm has potential for solving large-scale SDPs efficiently.

title: On The Significance Of Wigner’s Friend In Contexts Beyond Quantum Foundations
authors: Caroline L. Jones And Markus P. Mueller
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2147 (2026).

There has been a surge of recent interest in the Wigner's Friend paradox, sparking several novel thought experiments and no-go theorems. The main narrative has been that Wigner's Friend highlights a counterintuitive feature that is unique to quantum theory, and which is closely related to the quantum measurement problem. Here, we challenge this view. We argue that the gist of the Wigner's Friend paradox can be reproduced without assuming quantum physics, and that it underlies a much broader class of enigmas in the foundations of physics and philosophy. To show this, we first consider several recently proposed Extended Wigner's Friend scenarios, and demonstrate that some of their implications for the absoluteness of observations can be reproduced by classical thought experiments that involve the duplication of agents. Crucially, some of these classical scenarios are technologically much easier to implement than their quantum counterparts. Then, we argue that the essential structural ingredient of all these scenarios is a feature that we call "Restriction A": that a physical theory cannot give us a probabilistic description of the observations of all agents. Finally, we argue that this difficulty is at the core of other puzzles in the foundations of physics and philosophy, and demonstrate this explicitly for cosmology's Boltzmann brain problem. Our analysis suggests that Wigner's Friend should be studied in a larger context, addressing a frontier of human knowledge beyond quantum foundations: to obtain reliable predictions for experiments in which these predictions can be privately but not intersubjectively verified.

.
tldr: The paper argues that the Wigner's Friend paradox is not unique to quantum theory and can be reproduced classically, suggesting broader implications for foundations of physics and philosophy.
motivation: Recent interest in Wigner's Friend paradox has focused on quantum foundations, but the authors challenge the view that it is uniquely quantum, aiming to show its broader significance.
method: The authors analyze extended Wigner's Friend scenarios and construct classical thought experiments with agent duplication to reproduce the paradox, identifying a structural feature called 'Restriction A'.
result: They demonstrate that some implications of Wigner's Friend can be reproduced classically, and that the core issue is a limitation of physical theories to describe all agents' observations probabilistically.
conclusion: Wigner's Friend should be studied beyond quantum foundations, as it relates to puzzles like Boltzmann brains, addressing a frontier of knowledge where predictions cannot be intersubjectively verified.

title: Qubit Operations Using A Modular Optical System Engineered With PyOpticL: A code-to-CAD Optical Layout Tool
authors: Jacob Myers, Christopher Caron, Nishat Helaly, Zhenyu Wei, Justin Oh, Zack Gotobed, Kotaro Yabe, And Robert J. Niffenegger
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2135 (2026).

Complex optical design is hindered by conventional piecewise setup, which prevents modularization and therefore abstraction of subsystems at the circuit level. This limits multiple fields that require complex optics systems, including quantum computing with atoms and trapped ions, because their optical systems are not scalable. We present an open-source Python library for optical layout (PyOpticL) which uses beam-path simulation and dynamic beam-path routing for quick and easy optical layout by placing optical elements along the beam path without a priori specification, enabling adaptive, path-based layouts with automatic routing and connectivity. We use PyOpticL to create modular `drop-in' optical baseplates for common optical subsystems used in atomic and molecular optics (AMO) experiments including laser sources, frequency and intensity modulation, and locking to an atomic reference for stabilization. We demonstrate this minimal working example of a dynamic full laser system for strontium trapped ions by using it for laser cooling, qubit state detection, and over 99% fidelity single-qubit gates with 3D printed baseplates. This enables a new paradigm of design abstraction layers for engineering optical systems leveraging modular baseplates, as they can be used for any wavelength in the system and enables scaling up the underlying optical systems for quantum computers. This new open-source hardware and software code-to-CAD library seeks to foster open-source collaborative hardware and systems design across numerous fields of research including AMO physics and quantum computing with neutral atoms and trapped ions.

.
tldr: This paper presents PyOpticL, an open-source Python library for modular optical system design, and demonstrates its use for trapped-ion qubit operations.
motivation: Complex optical systems for quantum computing with atoms and trapped ions are not scalable due to conventional piecewise setup; a modular, code-to-CAD approach is needed.
method: The authors developed PyOpticL, which uses beam-path simulation and dynamic routing to enable adaptive optical layouts, and created modular baseplates for common AMO subsystems.
result: They demonstrated a full laser system for strontium trapped ions, achieving over 99% fidelity single-qubit gates with 3D-printed baseplates.
conclusion: PyOpticL enables a new paradigm of design abstraction for optical systems, fostering open-source collaborative hardware design for quantum computing and AMO physics.

title: Sorting Prolate And Oblate Spheroids With A Diatomic Gas In A Magnetic Field
authors: Ruben Lier
abstract: For a gas of diatomic particles with a nonzero magnetic moment, the Senftleben–Beenakker effect implies that transport can be affected by a magnetic field even when the particles are charge neutral. In such a gas, two independent anisotropic odd viscosities are allowed by symmetry and can have opposite signs. We study the resulting odd-viscous Stokes flow around spheroids in the regime where the odd viscosities are small compared to the shear viscosity. Using a perturbative expansion around the spherical solution and the Lorentz reciprocal theorem, we compute the lift forces on oblate and prolate spheroids for general values of the two odd viscosity coefficients. We show that the resulting Hall angles can differ for oblate and prolate spheroids, implying that sedimentation in a diatomic gas subject to a background magnetic field can separate particles according to shape.
tldr: This paper studies odd-viscous Stokes flow around spheroids in a diatomic gas under a magnetic field, showing shape-based separation via Hall angles.
motivation: Understanding how magnetic fields affect transport in neutral diatomic gases (Senftleben–Beenakker effect) and exploiting odd viscosities for particle separation.
method: Perturbative expansion around spherical solution and Lorentz reciprocal theorem to compute lift forces on spheroids for general odd viscosity coefficients.
result: Hall angles differ for oblate and prolate spheroids, enabling shape-based separation during sedimentation in a magnetic field.
conclusion: Odd viscosities in diatomic gases can be used to separate particles by shape, with potential applications in particle sorting.

title: Gravitational And Other Shifts Of Whispering-gallery And Gravitational State Interference Patterns Of Light Neutral Particles
authors: V V Nesvizhevsky, J A Pioquinto, K Schreiner, S Baeßler, P Crivelli, F Nez, S Reynaud, P Yzombard, S A Vasiliev And E Widmann
abstract: We discuss the interference patterns of gravitational and whispering gallery quantum states that can be observed with neutrons, atoms, antiatoms, muonium (Mu), positronium (Ps), and other light neutral particles. A gravitational shift of interference patterns of neutron gravitational and whispering-gallery states can be easily observed with cold, very cold, or ultracold neutrons. The developed methods can be used for observing/searching for other shifts in fundamental neutron physics experiments, for instance, for measuring the gravitational constant or constraining the neutron electric charge. A series of such measurements will be made with neutrons at the PF1B, PF2, D17 facilities at the ILL. A peculiar feature of analogous atomic (anti-atomic) experiments is the much smaller effective critical energies of the materials of mirrors for (anti)atoms. We evaluated parameters that make a measurement of the hydrogen and antihydrogen whispering-gallery states and their gravitational shifts feasible. A series of such measurements will be made with hydrogen and deuterium atoms by the GRASIAN collaboration in Vienna and Turku. A similar measurement with antihydrogen atoms may be of interest for the GBAR experiment, the ASACUSA experiment, which is producing a beam of slow antihydrogen atoms, and other experiments at CERN that study the gravitational properties of antimatter. Quantum reflection (QR) of Mu and Ps from material surfaces opens the possibility of observing whispering-gallery states, although such measurements remain experimentally challenging. Because of the small masses of Mu and Ps, their effective critical energies of the mirror materials are much higher for them than the effective critical energies for hydrogen and other atoms. The observation of gravitational shifts of such states is particularly demanding because of the extremely short lifetimes of these systems. Measurements of whispering gallery states with all these atoms and particles yield precise and detailed information on the QR properties of materials, providing valuable input for both fundamental physics and surface physics studies.
tldr: This paper discusses gravitational and whispering gallery state interference patterns for light neutral particles, focusing on experimental measurements of gravitational shifts and quantum reflection.
motivation: To explore gravitational and other shifts in interference patterns of quantum states for neutrons, atoms, and antiatoms, which could provide insights into fundamental physics and surface properties.
method: Theoretical analysis and experimental proposals for observing gravitational shifts of whispering-gallery and gravitational states using neutrons, hydrogen, antihydrogen, muonium, and positronium.
result: Parameters for feasible measurements are evaluated, and experimental setups at ILL, GRASIAN, and CERN are planned.
conclusion: These measurements can yield precise information on quantum reflection and gravitational properties, but the paper is primarily experimental and phenomenological, not advancing quantum information or thermodynamics theory.

title: Readjustment Of Intrinsic Activity Parameters Governs The Rectified Transport In Asymmetric Ratchets
authors: Yunyan Chen, Xiaoyuan Yu, Fengguo Li And Baoquan Ai
abstract: The rectified transport of active Brownian particles (ABPs) in asymmetric ratchets has been extensively studied. However, most existing literature regulates rectification by designing different structural boundaries. In this work, we shift the research perspective to the internal properties of ABPs and explore the influence of their internal physical parameters on the transport process. Using the vibration-driven vehicle (VDV) as a macroscopic experimental model for ABPs, we systematically adjust the overall mass and position of center of mass of the VDV to reveal its underlying dynamic mechanism. Through long-time dynamic tracking, we identify a ‘parameters readjustment effect’: an increase in mass weakens the particle’s average velocity and persistence length, ultimately driving the active system into a noise-dominated macroscopic localized state. More importantly, the shift of the center of mass induces persistent translational–rotational coupling in the VDV, leading to an anomalous non-monotonic reentrant phase transition in the rectification probability of the system. Our study reveals that this anomalous transport law is fundamentally governed by the dynamic spatial competition between the intrinsic chiral orbit radius of the VDV and the geometric characteristic scale of the channel. Coarse-grained ABP numerical simulations reproduce the overall experimental trends. This work indicates that load-induced parameters evolution is not merely a physical perturbation, but a core dimension that determines macroscopic transport behavior, providing physical insights and principles for going beyond purely geometric design constraints and designing efficient active rectification systems.
tldr: This paper studies rectified transport of active Brownian particles in asymmetric ratchets by adjusting internal parameters like mass and center of mass, revealing a 'parameters readjustment effect' and anomalous reentrant phase transitions.
motivation: Most existing work on active ratchets focuses on structural boundaries; this work shifts to internal properties of active particles to understand their influence on transport.
method: Experiments using a vibration-driven vehicle as a macroscopic model for active Brownian particles, combined with coarse-grained numerical simulations, systematically vary mass and center of mass position.
result: Increasing mass reduces average velocity and persistence length, leading to a noise-dominated localized state; shifting center of mass induces translational-rotational coupling causing non-monotonic reentrant phase transitions in rectification probability.
conclusion: Internal parameter evolution is a core determinant of macroscopic transport behavior, offering principles for designing efficient active rectification systems beyond geometric constraints.

title: Chiral Graviton Modes In Fermionic Fractional Chern Insulators
authors: Min Long, Zeno Bacciconi, Hongyu Lu, Hernan B Xavier, Zi Yang Meng And Marcello Dalmonte
abstract: Chiral graviton modes are hallmark collective excitations of fractional quantum Hall (FQH) liquids. However, their existence on the lattice, where continuum symmetries that protect them from decay are lost, is still an open and urgent question, especially considering the recent advances in the realization of fractional Chern insulators (FCI) in transition metal dichalcogenides and rhombohedral pentalayer graphene. Here we present a comprehensive theoretical and numerical study of graviton-modes in fermionic FCI, and thoroughly demonstrate their existence. We first derive a lattice stress tensor operator in the context of the fermionic Harper–Hofstadter (HH) model which captures the graviton in the flat band limit. Importantly, we discover that such lattice stress-tensor operators are deeply connected to correlation hole dynamics, readily generalizable to generic Chern bands. We then explicitly show the adiabatic connection between FQH and FCI chiral graviton modes by interpolating from a low flux HH model to a Checkerboard lattice model that hosts a topological flat band. In particular, using state-of-the-art matrix product state and exact diagonalization simulations, we provide strong evidence that chiral graviton modes are long-lived excitations in FCIs despite the lack of continuous symmetries and the scattering with a two-magnetoroton continuum. By means of a careful finite-size analysis, we show that the lattice generates an intrinsic decay rate for the graviton mode which is small compared to its energy. We discuss the relevance of our results for the exploration of graviton modes in FCI phases realized in solid state settings, experimental utility on diagnosis of fractional topological phases, as well as cold atom experiments.
tldr: This paper studies chiral graviton modes in fractional Chern insulators, a topic in condensed matter physics with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To determine whether chiral graviton modes, hallmark excitations of fractional quantum Hall liquids, exist in lattice fractional Chern insulators where continuous symmetries are broken.
method: Derives a lattice stress tensor operator for the Harper-Hofstadter model and uses matrix product state and exact diagonalization simulations to study graviton modes, including an adiabatic connection between FQH and FCI models.
result: Provides strong evidence that chiral graviton modes are long-lived excitations in FCIs despite lack of continuous symmetries, with a small intrinsic decay rate compared to energy.
conclusion: The results are relevant for experimental diagnosis of fractional topological phases in solid-state and cold-atom settings.

title: Vortex Solitons In Disclination Quasicrystals
authors: Hua Zhong, Yaroslav V Kartashov, Yongdong Li, Fangwei Ye And Yiqi Zhang
abstract: Quasicrystals are ubiquitous in nature. They represent unique aperiodic materials featuring long-range order that occupy an intermediate niche between exactly periodic and disordered materials. These properties are reflected in the unusual evolutionary dynamics of excitations and unique localization properties of linear eigenmodes supported by quasicrystals. In particular, being the structures characterized by discrete rotational symmetry of order , photonic quasicrystals can support the stable propagation of linear vortex-carrying light beams and vortex solitons. However, the impact of discrete rotational symmetry of quasicrystals on the properties of vortex light states has not been investigated so far, as only the systems constructed using the simplest Penrose tiling or corresponding optically induced Penrose lattices are considered in this context. Here, we propose a broad class of quasicrystals with global topological defects—disclinations—introduced into their structure that allows to produce novel quasicrystalline structures with any desired order of discrete rotational symmetry from the basic Penrose structure. Such global topological deformation substantially enriches the linear spectrum of quasicrystals, allowing them to support new types of linear vortex states and bifurcating from them families of stable thresholdless vortex solitons with unusual intensity and phase distributions. We find two different classes of stable vortex solitons comprising in-phase or out-of-phase pairs of closely located bright spots, with total intensity distribution reflecting a particular discrete rotational symmetry of the quasicrystal with disclination. Remarkably, even low-charge vortex solitons can be stable in quasicrystals with disclinations, whereas stability intervals for them broaden with the decrease of the discrete rotational symmetry of quasicrystals. Our results extend the theory of localization in quasicrystals to structures with global topological deformation, highlighting emerging prospects for the robust transmission of power or information arising in these systems.
tldr: This paper studies vortex solitons in photonic quasicrystals with disclinations, focusing on their stability and intensity distributions.
motivation: To understand how global topological defects (disclinations) in quasicrystals affect the properties of vortex light states, which have not been investigated before.
method: The authors propose a class of quasicrystals with disclinations, analyze their linear spectrum, and numerically find families of stable thresholdless vortex solitons.
result: Two classes of stable vortex solitons are found, with stability intervals broadening as discrete rotational symmetry decreases.
conclusion: The results extend localization theory to quasicrystals with topological deformations, suggesting potential for robust transmission of power or information.

title: Uniaxial-stress-induced Magnetic Transitions In The Triangular-lattice Antiferromagnet PdCrO2
authors: Nina Stilkerich, Tobias Ritschel, Hilary M L Noad, Richard Waite, Dmitry Khalyavin, Kousuke Ishida, Pascal Manuel, Fabio Orlandi, Seunghyun Khim, Elena Gati, Andrew P Mackenzie, Jochen Geck And Clifford W Hicks
abstract: Uniaxial stress is a promising method to tune magnetic frustration, allowing its effects to be studied in a precise way. In this work, uniaxial stress is applied to the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet PdCrO . The Cr–Cr magnetic interaction is very sensitive to interatomic separation, so laboratory-achievable stress can induce substantial changes in magnetic structure. Results from three types of measurement are presented: x-ray diffraction, the stress–strain relationship, and neutron diffraction. The combined data show that the elastic moduli of PdCrO are strongly affected by stress-induced changes in magnetic structure. A new, first-order stress-induced magnetic transition is observed, at which the lattice constant shrinks by 0.21%. The lattice stiffens dramatically across this transition: the Young’s modulus increases by GPa, and the Poisson ratio falls from to . This stiffening indicates that the magnetic order ‘locks,’ that is, becomes insensitive to lattice strain. This locking might occur because the new stress-induced magnetic order nests the Fermi surface of the Pd sheets. Other frustrated magnets, including candidate spin liquids, may show similarly strong coupling between magnetic and elastic degrees of freedom.
tldr: This paper studies stress-induced magnetic transitions in the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet PdCrO2, focusing on the coupling between magnetic order and elastic properties.
motivation: To understand how uniaxial stress can tune magnetic frustration and induce new magnetic phases in frustrated magnets.
method: Combined x-ray diffraction, stress-strain measurements, and neutron diffraction under uniaxial stress.
result: A first-order stress-induced magnetic transition is observed, accompanied by a 0.21% lattice shrinkage and dramatic stiffening of the lattice, indicating magnetic order becomes insensitive to strain.
conclusion: The strong magnetoelastic coupling suggests that similar effects may occur in other frustrated magnets, including candidate spin liquids.

title: Direct Visualization Of Field-driven Valence Band Modulation In Electrostatically Reconfigured Graphene Devices
authors: Umidakhon Rayimjonova, Chin-Yi Huang, Yi-Cheng Weng, Elin Cartwright, Fredrik O L Johansson, Noemi Vannucchi, Pavel Dudin, Avila Jose, Pei Ding, David Muradas-Belinchón, Henry Nameirakpam, Zhaojun Li, Andreas Lindblad And M Venkata Kamalakar
abstract: Graphene with ultrathin metal-oxide layers has emerged as a scalable platform for integrated electronic, spintronic, and neuromorphic devices. The in-plane electric fields in such devices are typically inferred indirectly from transport measurements, which do not provide microscopic details of the interface potential profile. Here, we use photoemission microscopy to uncover the precise electrostatic landscape of a complete device comprising diverse, heterogeneous ultrathin metal-oxide-covered graphene junctions. Using in operando x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy with submicron resolution, we directly image the real potential profile across an entire graphene device, including regions covered by AlOx and TiOx nanometer-thick overlayers. Tracking the valence band edge under current bias and gate voltage enables quantitative analysis of internal field evolution via a spectroscopic screening factor, revealing an up to more than 50% suppression of the electric field in graphene covered with oxides, in agreement with transport measurements. This demonstrates local reconfiguration of electric fields in graphene for advanced two-dimensional (2D) device engineering and circuitry, while our operando circuit spectroscopy measurements provide a generic means to uncover intricate potential landscapes and carrier redistribution in 2D electronic and spintronic circuits.
tldr: This paper uses photoemission microscopy to directly visualize the electrostatic potential profile in graphene devices with oxide overlayers, revealing field suppression.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic electrostatic landscape in graphene devices is crucial for optimizing electronic and spintronic performance, but indirect transport measurements lack spatial detail.
method: In operando x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy with submicron resolution was used to image the valence band edge across a graphene device under bias and gate voltage, extracting a spectroscopic screening factor.
result: The electric field in graphene covered with AlOx and TiOx is suppressed by up to 50% compared to bare graphene, consistent with transport measurements.
conclusion: Operando circuit spectroscopy provides a generic method to map potential landscapes in 2D devices, enabling advanced engineering of graphene-based circuits.

title: Phase-controlled Direct Laser Acceleration Enabled By Longitudinal Variation Of The Laser-driven Quasi-static Plasma Magnetic Field
authors: R Bhakta, I-L Yeh, K Tangtartharakul, L Willingale And A Arefiev
abstract: Direct laser acceleration (DLA) enables energy transfer from an ultra-high-intensity laser to plasma electrons and underpins many laser-driven particle and radiation-source concepts. A laser-driven azimuthal plasma magnetic field is a key player in this process: it confines energetic electrons, induces betatron oscillations, and makes possible a resonant interaction between the betatron motion and the laser field. While this betatron resonance can enhance electron energy gain, the gain itself generally drives frequency detuning and promotes largely reversible energy exchange that limits net acceleration. Here we show, using a test-electron model with prescribed fields, that a slow longitudinal increase of the quasi-static plasma magnetic field qualitatively changes DLA by introducing hysteresis in the ratio of the betatron frequency to the laser frequency experienced by the electron, so that this ratio depends on the prior evolution of the electron even at the same energy. This hysteresis enables phase control of the electron-laser energy exchange and suppresses the usual reversibility of DLA, allowing electrons to retain the acquired energy and sustain energy gain without intermittent losses.
tldr: This paper studies phase-controlled direct laser acceleration of electrons using a longitudinally varying plasma magnetic field, a topic in laser-plasma physics.
motivation: To overcome the reversible energy exchange that limits net acceleration in direct laser acceleration (DLA) schemes.
method: A test-electron model with prescribed fields is used to show that a slow longitudinal increase of the quasi-static plasma magnetic field introduces hysteresis in the betatron-to-laser frequency ratio.
result: The hysteresis enables phase control of the electron-laser energy exchange and suppresses reversibility, allowing sustained energy gain.
conclusion: Longitudinal variation of the plasma magnetic field can qualitatively change DLA dynamics, offering a new control knob for laser-driven particle acceleration.

title: Inferring The Underlying Higher-order Network Structure From Low-resolution Interaction State Data
authors: Chuang Ma, Xiao-Feng Luo, Rui-Hui He, Dao-Yu Li, Hai-Feng Zhang And Gui-Quan Sun
abstract: Network reconstruction aims to infer the underlying interactions between entities from observed data and serves as a cornerstone of network science. While most existing methods focus on dynamics-based data and primarily target binary interactions, real-world data often reflect coarse-grained interaction states of individuals over specific time intervals and may involve complex multi-body interactions beyond pairwise connections. Reconstructing the underlying higher-order network structure from such low-resolution interaction state data is therefore of critical importance. In this paper, we formulate an optimization model for inferring higher-order structures based on the minimum description length principle. To solve this problem, we propose a Bayesian network reconstruction method that integrates distribution estimation with Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling. Our method begins by generating candidate configurations for each time interval via MCMC sampling, then constructs a Bayesian network—guided by minimum-entropy—to capture dependencies between configurations across different time intervals. Finally, an iterative update strategy based on distribution estimation is employed to approach the optimal solution. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to infer higher-order network structures from low-resolution interaction state data using Bayesian networks and MCMC sampling.
motivation: Existing network reconstruction methods focus on binary interactions and dynamics-based data, but real-world data often involve coarse-grained interaction states and multi-body interactions.
method: The method formulates an optimization model based on the minimum description length principle, uses MCMC sampling to generate candidate configurations, constructs a Bayesian network guided by minimum-entropy, and iteratively updates via distribution estimation.
result: Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method for inferring higher-order network structures.
conclusion: The proposed Bayesian network reconstruction method successfully infers higher-order network structures from low-resolution interaction state data.

title: Characterizing The Low Energy Breakdown In Interpreting Photoionization Delays
authors: Brock Grafstrom And Alexandra S Landsman
abstract: Typical attosecond pump–probe experiments utilize a combination of extreme ultraviolet and IR laser pulses to extract precise timing information of electron dynamics. For sufficiently high photoelectron energies it is typically assumed that Wigner and Coulomb–laser-coupling (CLC) delays are separable, adding up to the experimentally measured photoionization delay. However, no widespread consensus has been reached on how to best interpret time delays at low photoelectron energies or IR wavelengths shorter than 800 nm. These questions are becoming crucial for the interpretation of state of the art ultrafast experiments in atoms and molecules studying electronic motion in bound and quasi-resonant states, where the dynamics of interest are typically only present within the low-energy portion of time delay spectra. In this work we provide an analytical cut-off law which describes the minimum energy where it is valid to approximate the total delay as the sum of the Wigner and CLC components for a given probe laser frequency. In doing so, we discover that the breakdown between the short-range (Wigner) and long-range (CLC) delay components begins around 23 eV for IR wavelengths near 400 nm. This energy is markedly higher than what is traditionally assumed, and therefore has important implications for interpretation of photoionization delay experiments probed with visible light.
tldr: This paper studies photoionization delays in attosecond pump-probe experiments, focusing on the breakdown of the separability of Wigner and Coulomb-laser-coupling delays at low photoelectron energies.
motivation: Interpreting time delays at low photoelectron energies or with short IR wavelengths is crucial for ultrafast experiments in atoms and molecules, but no consensus exists on how to separate delay components.
method: The authors derive an analytical cut-off law that defines the minimum energy where the total delay can be approximated as the sum of Wigner and CLC components, and apply it to various probe laser frequencies.
result: The breakdown between short-range and long-range delay components begins around 23 eV for IR wavelengths near 400 nm, which is higher than traditionally assumed.
conclusion: The findings have important implications for interpreting photoionization delay experiments probed with visible light, especially in the low-energy regime.

title: Deterministic Initiation Of Inner-shell X-ray Lasers By Two-color Raman Driving
authors: Carles Serrat
abstract: Inner-shell x-ray lasers are conventionally initiated by amplified spontaneous emission (ASE), so that the temporal onset and longitudinal phase of the emitted field are determined by microscopic noise fluctuations. As a result, the early-time dynamics of the laser pulse are intrinsically stochastic. We analyze a regime in which the initial polarization that triggers inner-shell x-ray lasing is imposed deterministically by a resonant two-color Raman drive. Two coherent x-ray fields at angular frequencies and satisfying induce a core–valence coherence at the lasing frequency through an off-resonant Raman coupling mediated by virtual intermediate states. No electromagnetic field is applied at , and population inversion is generated independently by conventional inner-shell photoionization. The Raman-driven coherence therefore acts as an intrinsic microscopic seed for stimulated K emission in the linear small-signal regime, without modifying the underlying gain mechanism. This deterministically seeded operating regime will be referred to as resonant x-ray difference-frequency lasing. Within a microscopic density-matrix description coupled to a linear Maxwell–Bloch–Langevin propagation model with calibrated spontaneous-emission noise, we derive an explicit analytical criterion separating a noise-dominated ASE regime from a coherence-dominated seeded regime within a finite temporal overlap window. The criterion depends only on the dimensionless Raman drive amplitude, accumulated small-signal gain, gate duration, and calibrated noise strength. Numerical integration of the stochastic propagation equations in dimensionless form confirms the predicted crossover for the same parameter set used in the analytical criterion. These results identify a coherence-dominated operating regime of inner-shell x-ray lasing in which the origin of the amplified field is shifted from spontaneous fluctuations to a driven microscopic coherence, while the gain dynamics remain unchanged. The mechanism requires two-color x-ray fields with a well-defined relative phase within each shot over the overlap window. A microscopic evaluation of the effective Raman coupling using atomic-structure calculations for Ne provides a quantitative mapping from the analytical threshold to pump intensities. Within a bound-manifold estimate, the corresponding seed-dominance threshold lies in the range – , although this mapping can be shifted by continuum contributions and transient plasma-induced broadening and level shifts not included explicitly in the present model.
tldr: This paper proposes a deterministic seeding mechanism for inner-shell x-ray lasers using two-color Raman driving, shifting the lasing onset from stochastic noise to a driven coherence.
motivation: Conventional inner-shell x-ray lasers are initiated by amplified spontaneous emission (ASE), leading to stochastic temporal onset and phase. The authors aim to achieve deterministic control over the lasing process.
method: The authors analyze a regime where a resonant two-color Raman drive induces a core-valence coherence at the lasing frequency, acting as a seed. They use a microscopic density-matrix description coupled to a linear Maxwell-Bloch-Langevin propagation model with calibrated spontaneous-emission noise, and derive an analytical criterion separating noise-dominated from coherence-dominated regimes.
result: An explicit analytical criterion is derived, depending on Raman drive amplitude, small-signal gain, gate duration, and noise strength. Numerical integration confirms the predicted crossover. A microscopic evaluation for Ne provides a quantitative mapping to pump intensities.
conclusion: The mechanism enables a coherence-dominated operating regime for inner-shell x-ray lasing, where the amplified field originates from a driven microscopic coherence rather than spontaneous fluctuations, offering deterministic control over the laser initiation.

title: Measurement Incompatibility And Quantum Steering Via Linear Programming
authors: Lucas E. A. Porto, Sébastien Designolle, Sebastian Pokutta, And Marco Túlio Quintino
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2141 (2026).

The problem of deciding whether a set of quantum measurements is jointly measurable is known to be equivalent to determining whether a quantum assemblage is unsteerable. This problem can be formulated as a semidefinite program (SDP). However, the number of variables and constraints in such a formulation grows exponentially with the number of measurements, rendering it intractable for large measurement sets. In this work, we circumvent this problem by transforming the SDP into a hierarchy of linear programs that compute upper and lower bounds on the incompatibility robustness with a complexity that grows polynomially in the number of measurements. The hierarchy is guaranteed to converge and it can be applied to arbitrary measurements – including non-projective POVMs (Positive Operator-Valued Measures) – in arbitrary dimensions. While convergence becomes impractical in high dimensions, in the case of qubits our method reliably provides accurate upper and lower bounds for the incompatibility robustness of sets with several hundred measurements in a short time using a standard laptop. We also apply our methods to qutrits, obtaining non-trivial upper and lower bounds in scenarios that are otherwise intractable using the standard SDP approach, although such bounds are significantly looser than the ones obtained in the qubit case. Finally, we show how our methods can be used to construct local hidden state models for states (i.e., to prove that a state cannot lead to steering under any possible local measurements), or conversely, to certify that a given state exhibits steering; for two-qubit quantum states, our approach is comparable to, and in some cases outperforms, the current best methods.

.
tldr: Analysis failed

title: Propagation And Collisionless Damping Of Topologically-protected Surface Plasma Waves In Non-uniformly Magnetized Plasma Columns
authors: Roopendra Singh Rajawat And Gennady Shvets
abstract: Recent theoretical studies revealed the existence of topologically-protected surface plasma waves (TSPWs) in uniformly magnetized cold plasma columns. Reflections-free propagation of the TSPWs along arbitrarily-shaped plasma boundaries oriented perpendicularly to the magnetic field was shown to be preserved even when their collisionless damping by localized upper-hybrid resonances was accounted for. Here we extend this theory to the realistic case of three-dimensional magnetic field produced by finite-sized magnetic coils. We demonstrate that when TSPWs are launched in the direction of the decreasing magnetic field, they are collisionlessly absorbed within a highly localized (evanescent) region as they propagate away from the magnetic coil.
